idiom_name: enum with associated values plus a custom init(from:) switching on the type key
implementation_notes: Swift models the choice as an enum with associated values - exhaustiveness checking is the dispatch table - and Codable supplies the wire half: when the format fixes a discriminator key, implement init(from:) on the wrapper, read the tag from a keyed container and switch to the concrete Decodable type, mirroring that in encode(to:). Decode the payload from the same decoder rather than from a container you already consumed, because keyed containers are views that do not advance it. The classic class hierarchy plus registry is only needed when the type set is loaded at runtime (plugins, dynamically registered messages) instead of compiled into the binary.
pitfalls: Decode the body from the same decoder, not from a nested container that was already read; mixing the two (or using superDecoder) re-reads members and produces confusing keyNotFound errors.
An unknown tag is thrown from deep inside the call stack as a DecodingError, so catch it at the boundary when you want one quarantined message instead of a failed batch.
Switching on a raw String loses exhaustiveness; declare the tag as a String-backed enum so adding a case makes every switch fail to compile.
